newsitem.title: UK: UK's Heseltine attacks Labour over trade unions.
newsitem.headline: UK's Heseltine attacks Labour over trade unions.

text.p: British deputy prime minister Michael Heseltine on Tuesday attacked the Labour Party's relationship with trade unions and said it had become a central issue in the May 1 election campaign.
"If Labour and the unions win, all of us will lose," Heseltine told a news conference.

A Daily Mail report on Tuesday claimed that if Labour won the election, 63 companies in Britain would be targeted by trade unions to exploit what it said were Labour plans to impose compulsory union recognition.
Heseltine said the key to Labour's plans was that union recognition could be voted in by small sections of any one company.
"Companies will become battle grounds in which different unions with separate agendas fight out historic rivalries and enmities, each seeking their own toehold on power," he said.
